lab-00.intent_label: Deliberately absurd or surreal comedy where nonsense is the point (sketch shows, anti-humor). Generic family animation or merely bad films are wrong.

lab-01.intent_label: Ambiguous: films directed by Andrei Tarkovsky first, then contemplative, poetic, spiritual cinema in his style.

lab-02.intent_label: Series centered on cooking or food with a warm, upbeat, low-conflict tone. Home renovation or dramas with incidental food are wrong.

lab-03.intent_label: Horror set in space or off-world with gradual, atmospheric dread rather than nonstop action.

lab-04.intent_label: Suspenseful planned-theft thrillers with a playful or hopeful tone; relentlessly hopeless crime stories violate the exclusion.

lab-05.intent_label: Stories centrally about a parent's grief after a child's death and its aftermath. Generic sadness or missing-child thrillers are weak.

lab-06.intent_label: Ambiguous mood vs title lookup: rage-driven, ferocious, high-intensity titles; the Fast & Furious franchise is a plausible title reading.

lab-07.intent_label: Unresolved typo (probably "crazy"); if read as crazy, eccentric or chaotic entertainment. Excluded from decisive scoring.

lab-08.intent_label: Mysteries where a lighthouse keeper matters to the story, with a wistful or sorrowful tone. A lighthouse as backdrop only is weak.

lab-09.intent_label: Science fiction where cars, driving or road vehicles are material (post-apocalyptic roads, flying cars, deadly races).

lab-10.intent_label: Literal clue: sunglasses worn at night are a notable feature (They Live, The Matrix), or cool nocturnal style; generic night imagery is weak.

lab-11.intent_label: Fantasy where real dragons appear and matter. "Dragon" in a name or martial-arts metaphor is wrong.

lab-12.intent_label: Other time-loop / repeating-day stories, ideally comedic or about personal growth. Groundhog Day itself is a reference hit, not a discovery.

lab-13.intent_label: Time travel with intricate causality, paradoxes or interlocking timelines; simple time-travel comedies are partial.

core-02.intent_label: Title lookup: Breaking Bad (the series) first.

core-03.intent_label: Title lookup: The Matrix (1999) first, sequels after.

core-06.intent_label: Suspenseful titles (thrillers, mysteries, competitions) that do not leave a hopeless aftertaste.

core-07.intent_label: Car chases are central to the experience: pursuit-driven action, getaway and road films.

core-08.intent_label: Sunglasses are a notable visual element or plot device (They Live, The Matrix, Men in Black).

core-09.intent_label: The narrator or viewpoint character is revealed to be untrustworthy, recontextualizing the story.

core-10.intent_label: Dark or satirical comedy where wealth and wealthy people are the target.

core-11.intent_label: Gritty, grounded crime series. Anime and movies are explicit exclusions.

core-12.intent_label: Titles that work across generations; no implicit content filter beyond broad appeal.

core-13.query: I want something tense that keeps me guessing, but I don’t want to finish it feeling miserable.
core-13.intent_label: Suspense and twists (mysteries, whodunits, clever thrillers) with a satisfying, not miserable, ending.

core-14.query: Rich people being absolutely awful to each other, preferably funny.
core-14.intent_label: Wealthy people behaving badly, comedy preferred (satire, black comedy).

core-15.query: A crime show that feels grubby and real. No animation, and nothing where the detective has magic powers.
core-15.intent_label: Grounded, gritty crime series; animation, supernatural detectives and movies are wrong.

core-16.query: Something where halfway through you realise the person telling the story has been feeding you nonsense.
core-16.intent_label: A revealed unreliable narrator is the core twist.

core-17.query: Give me car chases, but make it more getaway driver than superheroes destroying a city.
core-17.intent_label: Grounded getaway-driver and heist-driving films; superhero destruction spectacles are wrong.

core-18.query: Brain’s fried. Something warm and funny, but not painfully cheesy.
core-18.intent_label: Easy, warm comedies with wit, avoiding saccharine sentimentality.

core-19.intent_label: Comforting, gentle, low-stakes titles (warm animation, feel-good comedy).

core-20.intent_label: Deliberately bleak, despairing or harrowing titles.

core-21.intent_label: Strong comedies; broad, so quality and popularity should matter.

core-22.intent_label: Repeating time is the central mechanism.

core-23.intent_label: Contemplative, slow-paced, mood-heavy science fiction; loud action sci-fi is wrong.

core-24.query: a hopeful space adventure without horror
core-24.intent_label: Optimistic space adventures; space horror is an explicit exclusion.

core-25.query: something short to watch after work
core-25.intent_label: Short, low-commitment viewing (short films, brisk movies, episodic comedy); no exact runtime assumed.

core-26.query: Ich suche etwas Spannendes, das mich rätseln lässt, aber am Ende nicht völlig deprimiert.
core-26.intent_label: German: suspense and puzzles without a miserable finish.

core-27.query: Quiero una serie policial realista y cruda, sin animación ni detectives con poderes mágicos.
core-27.intent_label: Spanish: grounded gritty crime series; no animation or magic detectives.

core-28.query: Des gens riches qui se comportent horriblement entre eux, de préférence quelque chose de drôle.
core-28.intent_label: French: wealthy people behaving badly, comedy preferred.

core-29.query: Kafam çok yorgun. Sıcak ve komik ama aşırı duygusal olmayan bir şey izlemek istiyorum.
core-29.intent_label: Turkish: easy warm comedy, not overly sentimental.

new-01.intent_label: A robbery or theft carried out on or against a train is central. Trains without a heist, or heists without a train, are weak.

new-02.query: two geniuses in a battle of wits
new-02.intent_label: Cat-and-mouse between two brilliant opponents who outthink each other (detective vs criminal, rival magicians). A lone genius without a rival is weak.

new-03.query: satire about politics or big corporations
new-03.intent_label: Comedies that skewer politicians, lobbyists, media or corporations.

new-04.query: quiet and lonely in deep space
new-04.intent_label: Contemplative sci-fi about isolation far from Earth: solitary astronauts, long voyages, stations. Loud space opera is wrong.

new-05.intent_label: Cyberpunk set in dense, rain-soaked, neon-lit cities; tech-noir atmosphere matters.

new-06.intent_label: Martial-arts films where comedy is central (Jackie Chan, Stephen Chow). Serious martial-arts dramas are partial at best.

new-07.intent_label: Anime about simulated reality, cyberspace, or AI and identity. The live-action Matrix films themselves are not the answer.

new-08.query: like Breaking Bad but a comedy
new-08.intent_label: Crime series about an ordinary person drifting into crime, played for laughs. Pure dramas like Breaking Bad itself are weak.

new-09.intent_label: Science-fiction action released in the 1980s. Modern remakes are wrong on era.

new-10.intent_label: 1990s crime films celebrated for their writing and dialogue.

new-11.intent_label: Comedies where no romance plot drives the story; romantic comedies violate the exclusion.

new-12.query: war movie that isn't about World War II
new-12.intent_label: War films about Vietnam, WWI, Lebanon, modern conflicts, etc. WWII films violate the exclusion.

new-13.intent_label: Idea-driven science fiction for grown-ups; kid-oriented or pure spectacle sci-fi is wrong.

new-14.query: good first anime for someone who never watched anime
new-14.intent_label: Accessible, widely acclaimed anime that work as an entry point. Niche, fan-service or long-lore-dependent titles are wrong.

new-15.intent_label: The story is told out of chronological order and the structure is part of the experience.

new-16.query: whole movie takes place in one room
new-16.intent_label: Single-location films (one room, apartment, booth) that sustain drama through dialogue or tension.

new-17.intent_label: Reality-twisting, puzzle-box or surreal films that leave you rethinking what you saw.

new-18.intent_label: Kind, warm, uplifting titles without cynicism or cruelty.

new-19.query: A crew of misfits on a beat-up spaceship taking odd jobs on the edge of the law, lots of banter and found family, more fun than grim.
new-19.intent_label: Space-western / ragtag-crew adventures with humor and found family. Grim space horror is wrong.

new-20.query: An ordinary guy slowly realises his whole life is staged or fake and has to decide whether to break out of it.
new-20.intent_label: Protagonist discovers his reality is constructed (staged show, simulation, manipulated city) and confronts it.

new-21.query: un dessin animé drôle pour toute la famille
new-21.intent_label: French: funny animated films for the whole family. Adult animation or animated war dramas are wrong.

new-22.query: Antikriegsfilm, der zeigt, wie sinnlos Krieg ist
new-22.intent_label: German: anti-war films that show the futility of war. Heroic war spectacle is wrong.

new-23.query: psycological thriler with a big twist
new-23.intent_label: Misspelled "psychological thriller": mind-game thrillers built around a major twist.

new-24.intent_label: Guardrail title lookup: the 2011 Hunter x Hunter series first (1999 series acceptable next).

new-25.intent_label: Guardrail title lookup: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion first, related films/seasons after.

ho2-01.intent_label: Horror (supernatural or creature) set aboard a submarine or deep-sea vessel. Plain submarine war thrillers without horror are only loosely relevant; horror set elsewhere is wrong.

ho2-02.intent_label: Comedies whose main setting is a prison or jail. Serious prison dramas are wrong; comedies with only a brief jail scene are loosely relevant.

ho2-03.intent_label: Anime (Japanese animation) centered on pirates, on the sea or in space. Live-action pirate films are wrong; anime without pirates is wrong.

ho2-04.intent_label: Westerns that bring a samurai or Japanese swordsman into the frontier setting, or samurai films styled as westerns. A plain western or a plain samurai film is only loosely relevant.

ho2-05.intent_label: War films where a sniper or sniper duel is the central focus. Generic war films are loosely relevant; non-war sniper thrillers only loosely.

ho2-06.query: like Band of Brothers but about Vietnam
ho2-06.intent_label: Grounded, soldier-level Vietnam War films or series with the ensemble realism of Band of Brothers. WWII titles are wrong (that is the thing being swapped out).

ho2-07.query: like The Sopranos but in Italy
ho2-07.intent_label: Prestige organized-crime drama set in Italy (Camorra, Mafia, Roman crime), serious and character-driven. American mob stories are only loosely relevant.

ho2-08.intent_label: Whimsical, visually playful European (especially French) films with quirky characters and a fairy-tale tone, in the vein of Amélie and Jeunet. Amélie itself is fine but not required at the top.

ho2-09.intent_label: Space-set adventure or drama with human-only (or robot/AI) antagonists and no alien species. Titles built around alien races contradict the constraint.

ho2-10.query: animated movie that is not for kids
ho2-10.intent_label: Animated feature films made for adults: mature themes, violence, or serious subject matter. Family and children's animation contradicts the constraint.

ho2-11.intent_label: Tense, confined thrillers or horror set in Arctic or Antarctic isolation (research stations, ice-locked ships). Warm adventure or nature documentaries are wrong.

ho2-12.query: lazy sunny summer on the Italian coast
ho2-12.intent_label: Relaxed, sun-drenched stories set during an Italian summer by the sea, with a languid or romantic mood. Mafia crime or thrillers with heavy tension are only loosely relevant.

ho2-13.intent_label: Conspiracy and surveillance thrillers from the 1970s with a paranoid mood. Modern conspiracy thrillers are only loosely relevant; 70s thrillers without conspiracy only loosely.

ho2-14.intent_label: British crime comedies about gangsters from the 2000s, fast and funny. 1990s entries like Lock, Stock are close but slightly off-era; serious gangster dramas are loosely relevant.

ho2-15.intent_label: Films directed by Terry Gilliam first, then surreal, darkly comic fantasy in his style.

ho2-16.intent_label: Films starring Jackie Chan, especially his stunt-heavy martial-arts action comedies. Other martial-arts stars are loosely relevant.

ho2-17.query: A small-town cop who is way out of their depth investigates a murder, told with dry dark humour and lots of quirky locals.
ho2-17.intent_label: Crime stories with dark comedy centered on a small-town police officer facing a murder case and eccentric locals. Grim procedurals without humour are loosely relevant; broad slapstick cop comedies loosely.

ho2-18.query: A soldier comes home from war and can't fit back into ordinary life. I want it honest and quiet, not an action movie.
ho2-18.intent_label: Quiet, character-driven dramas about veterans returning home and struggling to readjust. Combat-heavy action films contradict the request.

ho2-19.query: Una comedia absurda sobre la vida en la oficina, con personajes ridículos.
ho2-19.intent_label: Spanish: an absurd comedy about office life with ridiculous characters. Workplace comedies set in offices; non-office comedies are loosely relevant.

ho2-20.intent_label: Grand-scale films or series with sweeping stories, big battles or journeys (historical, fantasy or sci-fi epics). Small, intimate stories are wrong.

ho2-21.intent_label: Typo for 'dystopian death game series': shows (series preferred) where people are forced into deadly games in a dystopian or trapped setting. Films of the same kind are good.

ho2-22.intent_label: Guardrail title lookup: The Expanse (2015 series) first.

ppl-01.intent_label: Comedies starring Brad Pitt first (dark or caper comedy counts). His serious dramas are loosely relevant; comedies without him are only loosely relevant.

ppl-02.intent_label: Action films starring Keanu Reeves first. Other action films with a similar feel are loosely relevant; his non-action roles are weak.

ppl-03.intent_label: Comedies where Bill Murray plays his dry, deadpan persona first. Other deadpan comedies without him are loosely relevant.

ppl-04.intent_label: War films and series with Tom Hanks in the cast first. War films without him are loosely relevant; his non-war films are wrong.

ppl-05.intent_label: Films directed by Steven Spielberg in the 1970s and 1980s first. His later films are loosely relevant; other directors' films are weak.

ppl-06.intent_label: Typo for Leonardo DiCaprio: thrillers starring him first. His romances and period dramas are weak.

ppl-07.intent_label: Kung-fu comedies directed by or starring Stephen Chow first. Other kung-fu comedies (e.g. Jackie Chan) are loosely relevant.

ppl-08.query: lustige Filme mit Bud Spencer und Terence Hill
ppl-08.intent_label: German: comedic brawler westerns and action comedies with the Bud Spencer and Terence Hill duo first. Films with only one of them come next.

ppl-09.intent_label: Style query: some Tarantino films welcome, but mostly other films with his feel: stylized violence, pop-culture talk, crime ensembles, nonlinear plots.

ppl-10.intent_label: Style query: one or two Wes Anderson films welcome, but mostly other whimsical, symmetrical, deadpan and pastel-hued films by others.

ppl-11.query: like david lynch but less weird
ppl-11.intent_label: Style query: Lynch's dreamy small-town darkness and mystery, but accessible and coherent. His most surreal films are wrong; Twin Peaks-like mysteries by others are ideal.

ppl-12.query: something in the style of guy ritchie
ppl-12.intent_label: Style query: some Guy Ritchie films welcome, but mostly other fast, witty British crime capers with ensembles of crooks.

ppl-13.intent_label: Style query: some Villeneuve films welcome, but mostly other brooding, slow, visually vast and tense sci-fi or thrillers.

ppl-14.intent_label: Style query: some Coen brothers comedies welcome, but mostly other dark, deadpan comedies about hapless people and botched crimes.

ppl-15.intent_label: Style query: some Miyazaki films welcome, but mostly other hand-drawn, gentle, nature-loving fantasy animation by others.

ppl-16.intent_label: Style query: some Kubrick films welcome, but mostly other cold, meticulous, unsettling films with striking symmetric imagery.

ppl-17.intent_label: Shows and films created or written by Vince Gilligan first, then tense, morally grey crime dramas in his style.

ppl-18.intent_label: Films directed by Christopher Nolan first, then cerebral, puzzle-box blockbusters in his style.

ppl-19.intent_label: Films starring Jim Carrey first, both rubber-faced comedies and his dramatic turns. Similar comedies without him are loosely relevant.

ppl-20.intent_label: Films directed by Edgar Wright first, then kinetic, genre-mashing British comedies in his style.

ppl-21.intent_label: Studio Ghibli films first. Similar Japanese fantasy animation from other studios is loosely relevant.

ppl-22.intent_label: Horror films released by A24 first. Other elevated, slow-burn arthouse horror is relevant; mainstream slasher franchises are weak.

ppl-23.intent_label: Pixar feature films first. Animated films from other studios (DreamWorks, Blue Sky) are only loosely relevant.

ppl-24.intent_label: Acclaimed HBO drama series first. Prestige dramas from other networks in the same vein are relevant but lower.

sty-01.query: feels like a terry gilliam film
sty-01.intent_label: Style query: some Terry Gilliam films welcome, but mostly other dark, surreal, visually baroque fantasies and dystopias with absurd humor.

sty-02.intent_label: Style query: some films written or directed by Charlie Kaufman welcome, but mostly other mind-bending, melancholic, meta comedies and dramas about identity and memory.

sty-03.intent_label: Style query (actor as style): some unhinged Nicolas Cage performances welcome, but mostly other over-the-top, gonzo action and thrillers with manic, scenery-chewing leads. His quiet dramas are weak.

sty-04.query: in the vein of mel brooks
sty-04.intent_label: Style query: some Mel Brooks films welcome, but mostly other genre parodies and spoofs with rapid-fire gags and slapstick.

sty-05.intent_label: Style query (studio): some Aardman films welcome, but mostly other gentle, dry, very British family comedies and stop-motion with sight gags and whimsy.

sty-06.intent_label: Style query, series only: shows with David Fincher's feel: cold, meticulous, dark procedural crime and psychological tension. His series welcome; films are weak.

sty-07.intent_label: Animated series created by Matt Groening first, then other satirical adult animated sitcoms in his style.

sty-08.query: un film à la jean-pierre jeunet
sty-08.intent_label: French: style query. Some Jeunet films welcome, but mostly other whimsical, quirky, visually inventive (often French) fantasies and dark fairy tales.

sty-09.intent_label: Style query: some Aronofsky films welcome, but mostly other intense, claustrophobic psychological dramas about obsession, addiction and mental unraveling.

sty-10.query: danny boyle movies and stuff like them
sty-10.intent_label: Films directed by Danny Boyle first, then other kinetic, energetic films with pulsing soundtracks and gritty, restless camerawork.

sty-11.query: jackie chan style stunts and slapstick
sty-11.intent_label: Style query (actor as style): some Jackie Chan films welcome, but mostly other martial-arts action comedies with inventive practical stunts and physical comedy.

sty-12.intent_label: Horror films produced by Blumhouse first, then other lean, low-budget, high-concept horror (found footage, home invasion, supernatural jump scares).
